document.description: betT (b0314) encodes the high-affinity choline transporter of Escherichia coli, a secondary carrier of the betaine/choline/carnitine transporter (BCCT) family driven by the proton-motive force. It has 12 transmembrane segments in the cytoplasmic membrane, with a short cytoplasmic N-terminus and a long cytoplasmic C-terminal domain. BetT activity rises about tenfold on hyperosmotic upshock, and C-terminal truncations block this activation. BetT supplies intracellular choline to the BetA-BetB pathway that makes the osmoprotectant glycine betaine. betT is transcribed divergently from betIBA, and both transcripts are induced by osmotic stress and choline.

document.description: betA (b0311) encodes the FAD-dependent choline dehydrogenase of Escherichia coli, a peripheral protein of the cytoplasmic membrane in the glucose-methanol-choline (GMC) oxidoreductase family. It oxidizes imported choline to betaine aldehyde with a respiratory (non-NAD) electron acceptor, the first of two steps by which E. coli makes the osmoprotectant glycine betaine from choline; the soluble NAD-dependent BetB enzyme performs the second step. The betIBA operon and the divergent betT choline-transporter gene are induced by osmotic stress and choline and repressed anaerobically by ArcA. betA mutants cannot use choline for osmoprotection but are rescued by glycine betaine. Crude membrane preparations also oxidized betaine aldehyde, but the purified enzyme oxidizes only choline.

review.summary: EC 1.2.1.8 (NAD+-dependent betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase) mapped from the HAMAP MF_00750 assignment of a second catalytic activity.
review.reason: The NAD+-dependent reaction belongs to BetB, not BetA. In the 1986 crude-membrane assay a membrane-bound, electron-transfer-linked activity oxidized both choline and betaine aldehyde; the NAD-dependent betaine-aldehyde oxidation in that paper was a separate soluble enzyme (BetB). GO:0008802 is defined by NAD+ as acceptor, so even the crude-membrane aldehyde activity would not fit it. Highly purified E. coli BetA oxidizes choline but fails to oxidize betaine aldehyde further (PMID:39510372). Acinetobacter baumannii BetA does oxidize betaine aldehyde in vitro (PMID:34431198), so aldehyde oxidation by BetA-family enzymes is contested. That paper does not name the acceptor; our inference is that it is not NAD+, because BetA is a GMC flavoprotein with an FAD site and no NAD-binding site. The UniProt entry lists the NAD reaction and the NAD/NADP Km values (0.06 and 0.5 mM), which the abstract assigns to the soluble enzyme; this is recorded as a source defect.

document.description: betB (b0312) encodes the NAD-dependent betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase of Escherichia coli, a soluble cytosolic enzyme of the aldehyde dehydrogenase superfamily. It oxidizes betaine aldehyde, made from choline by the membrane-bound BetA choline dehydrogenase, to the osmoprotectant glycine betaine. The purified enzyme is a homotetramer of 55 kDa subunits that is highly specific for betaine aldehyde, prefers NAD over NADP, and stays active at the high K+ concentrations found in osmotically stressed cells. betB is the middle gene of the betIBA operon, which is induced by osmotic stress and choline.

document.description: betA (PP_5064) encodes the FAD-dependent choline dehydrogenase of Pseudomonas putida KT2440, a GMC-family oxidoreductase in the betIBA glycine-betaine biosynthetic locus. It oxidizes choline to betaine aldehyde, passing electrons to the respiratory chain at the cytoplasmic membrane. The dedicated NAD-dependent BetB enzyme oxidizes the aldehyde to glycine betaine. In KT2440, betBA are required to convert choline to glycine betaine, for salt tolerance, and for growth on choline as a carbon or nitrogen source. Whether BetA-family enzymes also oxidize betaine aldehyde is contested: the purified E. coli enzyme does not, while Acinetobacter BetA does in vitro. In neither case is the reaction NAD-dependent.

review.summary: EC 1.2.1.8 (NAD+-dependent betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase) propagated by HAMAP MF_00750 as a second BetA activity.
review.reason: GO:0008802 requires NAD+ as acceptor. BetA is a flavoprotein that passes electrons to the respiratory chain, and no BetA-family enzyme has been shown to reduce NAD+. A. baumannii BetA oxidizes betaine aldehyde in vitro, but the paper does not name the acceptor; our inference is that it is not NAD+, because GMC flavoproteins carry FAD and have no NAD-binding site. Purified E. coli BetA, the source of the HAMAP second reaction, does not oxidize betaine aldehyde at all. The NAD-dependent step in KT2440 is performed by BetB (Q88CW7). This replaces the earlier UNDECIDED: the term is wrong for BetA whatever the status of that side reaction. The same call is made for E. coli BetA (P17444).

source_defects.explanation: HAMAP rule MF_00750 assigns the NAD-dependent betaine-aldehyde reaction (RHEA:15305, EC 1.2.1.8) to all BetA choline dehydrogenases. BetA is a respiratory-chain-linked flavoprotein; purified E. coli BetA does not oxidize betaine aldehyde (PubMed:39510372), and the aldehyde oxidation reported for A. baumannii BetA (PubMed:34431198) is, by inference from its FAD-only GMC fold, unlikely to use NAD+. The rule should drop EC 1.2.1.8, or replace it with an acceptor-linked reaction if one is demonstrated.

document.description: betB (PP_5063) encodes the dedicated NAD-dependent betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase of the betIBA operon. It irreversibly oxidizes betaine aldehyde, produced from choline by BetA, to glycine betaine while reducing NAD+ to NADH. The tetrameric potassium-binding enzyme performs the second consecutive step of glycine-betaine biosynthesis and supports osmoprotection in Pseudomonas putida KT2440.

review.summary: The reviewed UniProt record and KT2440 pathway literature agree that BetB catalyzes the irreversible NAD-dependent aldehyde-to-betaine step.
review.reason: This is the specific core molecular function of the dedicated BetB enzyme. The curated HAMAP rule MF_00804 (BADH) assigns the NAD-dependent betaine aldehyde to glycine betaine reaction and places the four catalytic residues (ACT_SITE 162, 252, 286, 464); NCBIfam TIGR01804 (BADH) agrees on family membership. In KT2440, betBA are genetically required for choline conversion to glycine betaine (PMID:17116241, abstract only); that is pathway-level evidence for the betBA pair, not a purified-BetB assay.
